The bounded review is complete. Those non-`out/` files are root's own harness inputs, written at session start; `work/` is byte-identical to what was supplied and no bare-`/tmp` write occurred.

## Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED — one item

**All five patch items are correct and I assent to each individually.** Aggregate assent to the exact 17-file hash set is withheld for one leftover in a file this patch already touches.

**Custody verified, nothing guessed:** 6839/6839 inventory clean; all five `afterSha256` match the supplied bytes; all five `beforeSha256` match the prior handoff's `finalV3Sha256`; the other twelve still equal v3; all five diff hashes verified.

**Behavioural scope independently confirmed.** `workflows_model.v1.py` executable AST is identical after stripping docstrings — and only a *leading* string-literal `Expr` is stripped, so any other literal change would still surface. `check_workflows.v1.py` loses exactly one control and gains none. The count effect is **measured, not inferred**: 1788 → **1787**, 0 failures each.

**On the substance**, I verified the newly published claims are true of the code rather than merely asserted — two distinct fingerprints differing only in `language`/`kind`/`discriminator` really do project to one row; that is a *disclosed coarsening*, not the ambiguity refusal (which still refuses); and `granularityWidenedToFile` really is present on a satisfied outcome and absent from a failing one. The coarsening cannot manufacture support, and the unsafe-repair gate remains the native `ClosedWorldV2`.

**BV6-V4-CR-1** — `check_workflows.v1.py` lines 711–716 still carry the rationale root itself declared false: *"`relation` is a CanonicalIdentifier, not an enum, so no keyword … can look up which registry."* It contradicts, in this same patch, the corrected schema description and §6. It's also too strong — the schema *could* enumerate the two relation names as consts; what it cannot do is dereference a registry. Remedy: restate as the deliberate choice. No control change needed.

**Three of my own claims corrected.** My v3 "no prose-substring controls" was false — one existed, and root is right to remove it. My v3 assent did not cover the 23:30/23:40 note additions; my last read was 23:26. And my v3 comparative baselines were wrong: identity **1345** and integration **388** per the retained v2 reports, not 1344/378 (378 was actually the v1 value).

I accept root's qualification that its eight outcome rows omitted bounds and so test matching only. My probe supplies bounds where an outcome is computed — but every fixture on both sides remains a synthetic helper fixture, the fingerprints are formatted labels rather than rehashed identities, and no closure admission is claimed.
